objective.statement: Replace written-out notes with the ornament sign that stands for them.
successCriteria: I find the main note of a written-out figure.
I see whether the extra notes go above, below or both, and how often.
I choose the sign: trill, turn, upper mordent or lower mordent.

explanation.text: A composer may write out an ornament in ordinary notes, as a group of small values. You may be asked to replace such a group by the ornament sign. First find the main note: the note the ornament decorates, which is usually the first or the last of the group. Then look at where the other notes are, compared with the main note.

Three notes: the main note, the note above, then the main note again, is an upper mordent. The same with the note below is a lower mordent. Four notes: the note above, the main note, the note below, the main note, is a turn. A longer group that alternates between the main note and the note above, often ending with the note below, is a trill.

Notice what the sign replaces. If you can see that a figure begins on the note below, it is a different, inverted pattern; you will not be asked about it. You are asked to replace written-out notes with a sign; you are not asked to write out the notes of an ornament from its sign. The sign must stand for exactly the notes shown.
Main note first. One extra note above (then back): upper mordent. Below: lower mordent. Above, main, below, main: turn. Long alternation with the note above: trill.

steps: F is the note above E.
E, F, E is an upper mordent.
demonstration.textAlternative: Written-out notes E F E: an upper mordent.

guided.prompt: The beamed group of short notes at the start of this bar (starting at the note marked A) is the written-out version of one ornament on the note B. Which ornament sign could replace the group?

music.textAlternative: A bass-clef stave, key signature of 3 sharps, 3/4. a note marked A in the space just above the stave; a note on the 5th line; a note in the space just above the stave; a note in the space above the 1st ledger line above the stave; a note on the 5th line.

hints: Find the main note, then see where the extra notes go.
Find the main note, then see whether the extra notes go above it, below it, or both, and how many times they alternate.

mistakes.upper-lower-mordent-swap: Check the direction: the upper mordent goes up to the note above; the lower mordent goes down to the note below.
mistakes.turn-inverted: A turn starts on the note above; an inverted turn starts on the note below.
mistakes.acciaccatura-appoggiatura-swap: Look for the slash through the small note: with it, the note is crushed in quickly (acciaccatura); without it, it takes time from the main note (appoggiatura).
mistakes.trill-mordent-confusion: A trill keeps alternating for the length of the note; a mordent is just one quick alternation.

feedback.fallback: Not quite. Compare the shape of the sign with each ornament's pattern.

mastery.completion: The lesson is complete when every step has been answered correctly (retries allowed). Only first-attempt, hint-free independent answers count as mastery evidence; guided steps never do.

provenance.authoredBy: Music Theory Path curriculum team (Brief 05, drafted with AI assistance; pending qualified teacher review)
provenance.notes: Original wording and original figures. Official outline: ornament assessment may ask for written-out notes to be replaced with signs, not for the realisation to be written from a sign. Only the four patterns a figure can identify are used; the small notes (acciaccatura, appoggiatura) cannot be told from a figure so they are not asked here.
